thread:
maria: Thanks everyone for joining the all-hands. Quick follow-up — can folks drop 1-2 bullet points about customer wins/losses from the last quarter and the single biggest ask we heard? I'll compile for the leadership Q&A doc. (pls keep short) :point_down:

sam: I'll go first. Win: enterprise retailer picked Dedicated for predictable latency and the on-prem option. They specifically cited our tail latency guarantees and canary rollback. Loss: Telco POC lost to vendor who had built-in Vector DB connectors. Ask: native connectors + better docs around integrations. —sam

anjali (cs): Win: fintech customer loved audit logs + KMS integration. Loss: onboarding time was longer than expected because they needed custom network config. Ask: onboarding playbook + runbook for Private installs.

leo (product): Noted. Add to roadmap backlog: connectors and onboarding guide. Also request from multiple accounts for per-route cost estimates in the Console.

cassie (sales): Quick note — wins tied to SLA language in contract + white-glove setup. Losses often price sensitivity on smaller deals (<$5k/mo). Ask: clearer starter pricing + a 'dedicated-lite' offering.

jordan (eng-rt): From infra side: wins = runtime perf wins after 2.3 kernel updates. Loss = occasional OOM on long-seq LLMs hit one POC. Action: create a perf checklist for long-context customers.

leah (eng-ml): Product-quality ask: customers want more predictable response quality across quantized models; we should add 'model-quality' profiles and recommended knobs. Example: recommend disabling extreme quantization for agents.

dev-bot: Poll opened: 'Which ask should be P0 for next sprint?' Options: connectors, onboarding playbook, per-route cost in Console, dedicated-lite. (react to vote)

maria: Thanks! I'm capturing all these. Will we assign owners? @leo for connectors, @jordan for perf checklist, @anjali for onboarding playbook, @cassie for pricing proposal.

sam: +1. Also want a one-pager for execs summarizing top 3 wins and top 3 losses for GTM. Maria, can you own it? timeline EOW?

maria: I can. EOW is tight but doable — will draft and share for comments. tagging @leah for quality profiles input.

anjali: I'll drop a short runbook template into #docs in 30m.

cassie: I'll surface pricing options with finance and post back tomorrow.

leo: Will add connectors spike to next sprint planning; estimate 2 weeks for design.

jordan: I'll write the perf checklist and a troubleshooting snippet:

```
# quick OOM mitigation
1) limit max_seq to 8k
2) enable KV prefix caching
3) route to longer-GPU nodes
```

leah: I'll put together model-quality sample configs and an eval checklist.

maria: Awesome. One more ask — please add any customer quotes or links to deal notes here. I'll include anonymized snippets in the one-pager.

cassie: Dropping one: 'Redwood's Dedicated brought our error rate down by 40% in production' — happy to share the slide.

sam: Thanks all. This is exactly the kind of feedback loop we want. We'll review in next leadership sync and prioritize.
